findings.diagnosis: The prompt treats function-word-led complements (prepositional phrases, subordinators, relative/participial openings, exception markers) as acceptable cut points rather than as parts that must stay attached to the predicate or nominal they complete, so separate-piece translations lose or flip essential time/place/argument/exception information.
findings.evidence: en_us_292, en_us_1116, en_us_101, en_us_1029, en_us_1062, en_us_525, en_us_487 — these 7 sentences all keep a cut immediately before a preposition/subordinator/relative/participial/exception phrase that supplies the main temporal, locative, argumental, or exception information for the preceding verb or noun, producing high contradiction or cohesion loss when the pieces are translated alone.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences where a preposition or subordinating/relative/participial/exception word (for example: a preposition, 'that', 'while', 'if', 'when', 'except', or a participial opener) immediately begins a phrase which supplies the main temporal, locative, argument, or exception complement of the immediately preceding verb or noun.

edit.text: Do not cut immediately before a preposition or a subordinating/relative/participial/exception opener (e.g. 'that','while','if','when','except') when it introduces the main time/place/argument/exception complement that completes the preceding verb or noun.
